workflow.name: Track EU tender deadline changes and send briefs with Apify and Slack
workflow.description:
## Quick overview
This workflow runs daily to fetch new and changed EU tender notices from the Apify EU Tenders Scraper (TED), maintains one tracked row per procedure in an n8n Data Table, and posts a single Slack morning brief highlighting changed deadlines/cancellations, due-soon reminders, and new tenders.

## How it works
1. Runs every day at 07:00 (or manually in a sample mode) and loads the configured filters and brief settings.
2. Pulls only new TED notices from the Apify EU Tenders Scraper (TED) Actor (or generates sample notices for a test run).
3. Merges the returned notices into an n8n Data Table keyed by procedure, updating existing rows for change notices and creating rows for newly discovered procedures.
4. Reads all tracked procedures and compiles a Slack-ready brief with three sections: Changed (including old vs. new deadlines and cancellations), Due soon (based on reminder day thresholds), and New.
5. Posts the brief to a Slack channel, splitting into multiple messages if needed to stay within Slack message length limits.
6. After Slack accepts each message, updates the corresponding Data Table rows to stamp which tenders were notified/changed/reminded so they are not reposted.
7. If the Apify search fails, hits the maxItems cap, or Slack rejects a message, stops the run so an Error Trigger posts a failure alert to Slack.

## Setup
1. Install the community node `@apify/n8n-nodes-apify` and add an Apify API token credential.
2. Add a Slack OAuth2 credential with `chat:write`, set the target channel in both Slack steps (brief and failure alert), and invite the Slack app to that channel.
3. Review and update the values in “Your settings” (countries, CPV codes, keywords, publishedWithinDays, maxItems, timezone, remindDaysBefore, and changeAlerts).
4. Ensure the workflow can create and access the n8n Data Table named `eu_tender_procedures` (it is created automatically on first run).
5. In n8n Workflow Settings, set the correct timezone and select this workflow as its own Error Workflow so the failure alert runs on errors.
6. (Optional) Run “Try it with sample notices” and change `sampleDay` to 2 to test change/deadline behavior without incurring Apify usage.

## Requirements
- n8n with Data Tables, and the Apify community node `@apify/n8n-nodes-apify`. Tested with: n8n 2.48.2 (Cloud), @apify/n8n-nodes-apify 0.9.0
- An Apify account
- A Slack workspace where your app may post

## Customization
- Change the trigger time, the reminder days (`remindDaysBefore`) or the time zone of the dates (`timezone`).
- Set `changeAlerts` to `deadline` to post only moved deadlines and cancellations.
- To follow a second market in another copy of the workflow, give that copy's Data Table a different name in its five table nodes.

## Additional info
Why it tracks procedures: TED publishes every change to a tender as a new notice with its own number. Of the 42,628 competition notices TED published from 13 October to 12 November 2026, 12,732 (30%) were changes to an earlier notice, and 8,538 of those moved the deadline by a day or more, nearly all of them later, by a median of 7 days. The share of changes differs by country, from 13% to 50% among the ten largest. A monitor keyed on the notice number posts such a tender again as new and keeps counting down to the deadline it saw first.

Limitations: a pause longer than `publishedWithinDays` misses notices; changing a filter starts a new "Only new notices" history; a tender with lots is one row, and the Actor reports the earliest lot deadline; award notices are not tracked. The table is read in full on every run, so the workflow suits a filtered market (a country, a CPV division), not all of TED. The Code nodes were tested with a day-by-day replay of 12,155 real notices.

Actor used: EU Tenders Scraper on Apify Store — https://kizukidata.com/go/eu-tenders/n8n
Questions or a custom feed: https://kizukidata.com/custom/

workflow.name: Track EU tender deadline changes and send a Slack brief with Apify

parameters.content:
### How it works
For bid teams that follow EU tenders on TED. TED publishes a change to a tender (a new deadline, corrected documents, a cancellation) as a new notice with its own number. From 13 October to 12 November 2026, 12,732 of TED's 42,628 competition notices (30%) were such changes, and two in three of them moved the deadline by a day or more. A monitor that treats every notice as a new tender posts those tenders again and reminds you of deadlines that were already replaced.

This workflow keeps one row per procedure in a Data Table. Every morning the EU Tenders Scraper (TED) Actor returns the notices that are new for **Your settings**; a change notice updates the row of its tender. Then one brief goes to Slack: **Changed** (old and new deadline, cancellations), **Due soon** (7 and 2 days before the current deadline) and **New**. Rows are stamped after Slack accepts each message, so the lines of a rejected message are sent again on the next run. A failed run posts an alert.

Limitations: a pause longer than `publishedWithinDays` misses notices. Changing a filter starts a new history: notices are returned and charged again. A tender with lots is one row, with the earliest lot deadline. Award notices are not tracked.

### Setup
1. Install the community node `@apify/n8n-nodes-apify` (https://docs.apify.com/platform/integrations/n8n). Add Apify and Slack credentials.
2. Set the channel in both Slack nodes and invite the app.
3. Try it without Apify: run **Try it with sample notices**. Set `sampleDay` to 2 and run it again.
4. Edit **Your settings**. In Workflow Settings, choose the Timezone and select this workflow as its Error workflow.
5. Activate.

Tested with: n8n 2.48.2 (Cloud), @apify/n8n-nodes-apify 0.9.0

### Customization
Change the trigger time, `remindDaysBefore` or `changeAlerts`.

## Try it first
**Try it with sample notices** sends five made-up tenders through the same nodes and posts the brief, with no Apify run. With `sampleDay` 2 it sends four change notices for them. The next real run retires the sample rows.

## Your settings
Filters: `countries`, `cpvCodes` (`72` is the whole division), `keywords`, `publishedWithinDays`, `maxItems` (keep it under 300). Comma-separated lists; an empty list keeps all. Brief: `timezone` (IANA name), `remindDaysBefore`, `changeAlerts` (`all` or `deadline`).

## Apify node and cost
USD 0.80 per 1,000 notices on the Free plan; a run stops at USD 0.25, about 300 notices. A change notice counts as a notice. Retry is off: a retried run could charge twice. Keep On Error on `Continue (using error output)`.

## The tenders table
One row per procedure, keyed by TED's procedure identifier. A change notice updates the row and puts the deadline Slack last showed in `previousDeadline`, so the brief can show old and new. Rows are never deleted. A tender already closed when first seen stays unposted.

## The morning brief
Needs a **Slack OAuth2 API** credential with `chat:write`. A line is posted once: its row is stamped after Slack accepts the message. A rejected message stops the run and is built again next time. A missed reminder day is sent on the next run.

## Failures
A failed Actor call, a run that returns `maxItems` notices (after saving and posting them) or a rejected Slack message fails the run. The Error Trigger then posts the node, error and link. It needs this workflow as its own Error workflow and skips manual runs.

data.details: In n8n, when a workflow execution fails, it can start another workflow. This second workflow can be any arbitrary workflow on your n8n instance. Use the Error Trigger node as your Trigger in the Error workflow.

The IF node can be used to implement binary conditional logic in your workflow. You can set up one-to-many conditions to evaluate each item of data being inputted into the node. That data will either evaluate to TRUE or FALSE and route out of the node accordingly.

This node has multiple types of conditions: Bool, String, Number, and Date & Time.
